From 3rd August, India's stock market gets a major upgrade Here's why it matters

SEBI is changing how the closing price of stocks is calculated

Earlier - Closing price = Average price of trades in the last 30 minutes (VWAP)

Now - Closing price = The price where the maximum buyers and sellers match in a closing auction.

Closing Price is the official final price of a stock at the end of the trading day

Example If a stock trades between ₹95 and ₹100 throughout the day, and the official closing price is ₹98, then ₹98 is used to calculate returns, mutual fund NAVs, indices, and F&O settlement.

Why does it matter? 
✅ Harder to manipulate prices
✅ Better price discovery
✅ More accurate mutual fund NAVs, indices & F&O settlement
✅ Brings India in line with global markets

One change massive impact

The closing price isn't just a number it decides index values, mutual fund NAVs, F&O settlement, and billions of rupees worth of portfolios every single day.

SEBI has just made that number more reliable

Why do some businesses become Nestle while others become Vodafone Idea?

From Empty Chairs to Expansion: The Business Life Cycle Through Riya’s Cafe

Riya’s Cafe began as a rented corner with more chairs than customers Sales were low, rent was high and every day ended in red

1) This was the Startup Stage  where you pay to learn before you earn

But slowly, things changed her cold coffee and cheese sandwiches became the talk of the neighbourhood office crowds walked in, Zomato ratings climbed, and discounts weren’t needed anymore

Sales rose, costs fell, and profits finally appeared

2) Welcome to the Growth Stage  where every extra customer adds real money to the till

A few years later, Riya owned three cafes across the city regular customers, smooth operations, supplier credit, predictable cash flows  everything ran like a system.

Growth cooled from 40% to 10%, but profits stayed strong and stable

3) This was the Maturity Stage leess chaos, more consistency.

But competition arrived new cloud kitchens ,trendy coffee chains footfall dropped while rent and salaries stayed the same

Now came the crossroads Let profits shrink? Or reinvent?

She could launch delivery only kitchens, build her own coffee brand, or turn one outlet into a co working cafe

4) This was the Decline or Extension Stage  where businesses either fade or fight for a comeback.

Every stock is just a Riya’s Café at some stage of this journey

Startup → Growth → Maturity → Decline/Extension

Because behind every stock ticker is a Riya’s Cafe a story in progress the smartest investors don’t just buy the company they buy the stage of the journey

Kartikey

My friend just bought an iPhone 16 and I thought I am broke😭  but I was wrong


So today, my best friend and I went to the store to check the price

The iPhone 16 was around ₹62,000

Then the salesman said,
"Sir just pay ₹4,000 today the rest is on easy EMIs"

For a moment, it actually felt affordable

On the way back, my friend said,

"Bro, iPhones are normal now you should buy one too"

He'll spend the next few years paying EMIs

I'll keep using my ₹8,000 second-hand phone

No EMI
No monthly stress
Just peace of mind

Sometimes the most expensive phone isn't the one with the highest price tag

It's the one that keeps taking money out of your pocket every month

Don't ask, "How small is the EMI?"

Ask, "Is this purchase helping my future, or borrowing from it?"

That's the difference between looking rich and becoming rich

A genuine question for Gen Z: Would you rather own an ₹8,000 phone with zero stress, or an iPhone with years of EMIs?


Kartikey

Reputation Attacks Can Become Financial Attacks

For banks, reputation is not just branding.
Reputation is operating capital

If public confidence gets shaken, the impact can move through deposits, stock price, investor sentiment and employee morale.

That is why personal vendetta driven narratives around banks are dangerous

If the target is an individual, but the damage is done to the institution, then the public pays the price

This is exactly why the HDFC bank narrative needs to be seen carefully One sided panic can become real financial damage
